chunks: "The requirement is that the gate has to be about ten volts above the source. The source is the switch node, which goes up to the motor supply.
So I need a gate supply that moves with the switch node. I'd use a half-bridge driver with a bootstrap.
There's a diode from the 10 volt driver supply to a boot pin, and a capacitor between the boot pin and the switch node.
When the low-side FET is on, the switch node is near ground and the capacitor charges to about 9. 6 volts through the diode.
When the high side turns on, the switch node rises to the supply, the capacitor holds its 9. 6 volts, so the boot pin sits 9.
6 volts above the switch node, and the driver's high-side output uses that to push the gate. Sizing: say the gate charge is 40 nanocoulombs.
To keep the droop under half a volt I need at least 80 nanofarads, so I'd pick about half a microfarad.
The diode has to block the supply plus the driver voltage, so a 60 volt fast Schottky for a 24 volt bridge.
I'd add a gate resistor of about 10 ohms with a small diode for fast turn-off, a 100 k resistor from gate to source so it stays off if the driver loses power, and dead time in the driver.
The limitation is that a bootstrap only refreshes when the low side is on, so for 100% duty I'd use a driver with an internal charge pump, or limit duty to about 98%."
